opportunities.title: Introduction to 3D Printing
opportunities.description: Learn how 3D printers work and how you can print at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class includes hands-on instruction with Prusa Slicer, the software used to prepare your 3D object file for printing on a Prusa MK3S+ & Prusa MK4S 3D printer. Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software. Registration is required. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
opportunities.description: A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level. Prerequisites: Computers for Beginners 1, 2 & 3 or basic mouse, keyboarding and internet skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet weekly, in-person, every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club every Tuesday and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For ages 6-12. Drop in. No registration required. Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Food may contain or have come into contact with common allergens. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. Upcoming programs: September 22 - Dash robots September 29 - Sphero robots October 6 - This or That quiz with iPads + poster craft Live or automated closed captioning, sign language interpretation, intervenor services, or attendant services are available upon request. Please submit your request at least 2 weeks in advance to: tpl.ca/accessibility-events.

opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For ages 6-12. Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. September: Marble Run Marble Run is a fun track where marbles roll down using gravity. Children can build tracks with tubes, ramps, and tunnels, then watch the marbles race to the finish. In this program, kids will explore, create, test, and improve their own marble runs. They will learn about gravity, speed, and problem-solving while having fun. Let's build, play, and discover together!

opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, Sept 8, 15, 22 and 29. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Coding with Python II
opportunities.description: Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics ad system scripting. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. We will also introduce some new data structures which, unlike variables, can hold more than one piece of data at a time. This class is for beginners but assumes you have a basic understanding of Python or have attended Coding with Python I. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class . This program is hosted on Zoom. The Zoom information and link will be shared over email. opportunities.title: Photo Editing with Photoshop
opportunities.description: Adobe Photoshop is the world’s best imaging and graphic design software and is at the core of just about every creative project, from photo editing and compositing to digital painting, animation, and graphic design. Join us for an introductory lesson and learn about the most common tools. We'll explore the workspace and enhance images while investigating tools such as crop, levels, colour balance and more. See how an image can be altered and repaired using patch tools such as the clone and healing brush tools. We'll also dive deep into the world of layers and how you can manage them for those really unique and fun projects. Registration is required. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, September 9, 16 and 23. Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Introduction to 3D Printing
opportunities.description: Learn how 3D printers work and how you can print at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class includes hands-on instruction with Prusa Slicer, the software used to prepare your 3D object file for printing on a Prusa MK3S+ 3D printer. Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software. Registration is required. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Kids Can Vote: Tree of the Year Craft
opportunities.description: Join us for an afternoon of tree themed crafts where we will be exploring "Tree of the Year" candidates as they relate to the Kids Vote Weekend. In this event, we will learn about elections, understand the impact of voting, and children are welcome to start their journey to becoming lifelong voters. Check out Kids Vote Weekend (KVW), a fun event hosted by Toronto Elections. Drop-in. Limited capacity. Toronto's municipal election takes place on October 26, 2026. Check out the KnowYourVote.TO website and the Celebrate Democracy page to learn more about the upcoming election, access important voter resources, and discover activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you. Generously supported by: McConnell Foundation.

opportunities.title: Generative AI for Small Business
opportunities.description: Join us online with Digital Main Street. As AI continues to evolve, how your business utilizes it for your online presence can also evolve your brand. In this webinar, you will learn about generative AI and the different ways it can help your business. The webinar will discuss best practices for applying it to your marketing strategies, various AI platforms, and the areas it can support your business. Attendees will walk away with a solid understanding of generative AI and how to integrate it with their existing marketing plans. GenAI Tools being explored: 1. Gemini 2. Gemini Notebook 3. Nano Banana Session Agenda: 1. What is Generative AI? 2. AI & Your Daily Operations 3. AI & Customer Support 4. AI & Marketing 5. Best Practices for AI: Challenges with Using AI and How to Mitigate Them This program is part of the Newcomer Entrepreneurship Initiative and our continued efforts to champion inclusive entrepreneurship in Toronto, by finding more ways to uplift and support the journeys of diverse entrepreneurial communities such as newcomer entrepreneurs, Black entrepreneurs, and women entrepreneurs. We strive to accomplish this through storytelling, shared experiences, and open conversations that reflect the diversity of Toronto’s small business community. Registration: This virtual Zoom event is free to join. Once registered, you’ll receive an email with the Zoom link. Need help with Zoom? - Joining and participating in a Zoom webinar - Zoom Privacy Statement Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. opportunities.title: Python Essentials 2 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Take an intermediate Python course to advance your programming skills. This learning circle will meet online on Thursday afternoons, 2-3:30pm for August 6 to September 24. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly to complete the course together. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Python Essentials 2 is designed for learners who are already familiar with the essentials of Python, including programming concepts like data types, containers, functions, conditions, and loops. Required: completion of the Python Essentials 1 course, or equivalent experience. Python Essentials 2 is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming , including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing, as well as general coding techniques and object-oriented programming (OOP). For more information about the Python Essentials 2 learning circle, please contact networkingacademy@tpl.ca Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.description: Join Family Services York Region for a practical Back-to-School Reset! This session is facilitated in Mandarin and is perfect for newcomer families. Gain tools for smoother transitions and balanced tech use. Participants will learn: How to establish healthy family routines. How to manage screen time. How to build positive digital habits that support your child’s success in schools. 開學了，如何幫助孩子收心？ 總是為了手機、電腦和孩子吵架？ 誠邀您參加 「 開學收心指南」實用講座！ 一起解鎖健康家庭作息、合理控管螢幕時間，培養健康的電子產品使用習慣。 *The program's facilitator also speaks Cantonese*

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Passive Worksheets (Wordsearches & Colouring) + Kapla Blocks & Challenge Cards + Guest Speaker Day speaker from City of Markham's Environmental Services, 11am-12 noon PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Markham Village
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity
opportunities.description: Want to learn how to add custom audio to your films and videos? Perhaps a voiceover? Join us in our Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity workshop! Audacity is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. Audacity is a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) that is FREE to download. This makerspace demonstration will provide instruction on how to use this program to get you started with sound editing and recording. We will cover how to edit sound, what effects this program has to offer on your vocals and how to mix down your different tracks. At the end of the session you will receive a quick tour of Markham Village's sound booth and more information on how to book the space. With your new skills, why not participate in our upcoming Markham Village Film Festival ? Hope to see you there. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified!
opportunities.address: Markham Village Branch, 6031 Highway 7, Markham, Ontario, L3P 3A7

opportunities.title: Digitizing & Restoring 35mm Slides with AI
opportunities.description: Learn how to preserve your memories by converting 35mm slides or negatives into high resolution digital images. This demonstration introduces the process of scanning 35mm slides, and AI-powered restoration/modification techniques to remove deterioration and correcting the images' colours. Participants will leave with the knowledge needed to begin digitizing and restoring their own slide collections. Learning outcomes: Learn how to scan and digitize 35mm slides (or negatives) using Makerspace equipment Use AI tools to enhance scanned images by correcting colour and removing common imperfections Note: Program may allow drop-in participants, if space allows. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified! Check out the other Digital Innovation Month Tours and Programs - all happening this month: Markham Village: Tour Demo - Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity Thornhill Community Centre Tour Demo - Digitizing & Restoring 35mm Slides with AI Aaniin Tour Workshop - Cricut - Make an MPL Canvas Tote Bag Angus Glen Tour Workshop - How to Laser Engrave a Wooden Magnet with The Glowforge (4/5 - Digital Innovation Month Makerspace Series) Cornell Tour Demo #1 - Creating a Customized Puzzle with a Sublimation Printer - 11am Demo #2 - Creating a Customized Puzzle with a Sublimation Printer - 3pm

opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.description: Join our G1-G2 level Tips and Fun with Math virtually, where students can sit comfortably at home while receiving classroom quality math deliverables, develop basic logic and arithmetic skills, a general understanding of geometry, and practice simple word problems! opportunities.title: Discover a Career in Science/Health Care
opportunities.description: Are you interested in starting a career in the field of health care? Or perhaps you work in the health care field and are looking to add to your education to move into a new area of health care? We’ll highlight important things such as: We will cover programs such as Personal Support Worker, Practical Nursing, Registered Nursing and Medical Device Reprocessing We will cover programs in the field of Science We will touch on entrance requirements, steps to apply A bit about financial aid and student supports **Please note: This workshop is run in partnership with Seneca Polytechnic**. _______ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.
opportunities.address: Markham Village Branch, 6031 Highway 7, Markham, Ontario, L3P 3A7

opportunities.title: Be An Active Digital Citizen - Play-based Workshop for Families
opportunities.description: In this play-based, interactive workshop for children and families, we explore what it means to be a smart, safe, and empowered digital citizen. Through games and hands-on activities, children will practice healthy social media habits and learn about their digital rights online in a fun, age-appropriate way. At the end of this workshop, participants should: Be able to recognize healthy vs. unhealthy social media habits and practice simple strategies for balanced use. Understand basic digital rights for children online (i.e. privacy, safety, expression). Build confidence identifying safe, respectful ways to engage with others online, both individually and as a family. Note: this session is intended to be intended by families including children aged 8 - 16 and their parents/caregivers . Please register for each individual attending. Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.title: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams
opportunities.description: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams which addresses the growing threat of AI-enabled online fraud and scams targeting older Canadians. As AI tools become more accessible, scammers are using tactics such as voice cloning, deepfake videos, and highly convincing phishing techniques to impersonate loved ones and fabricate financial emergencies. Older adults aged 55+ are disproportionately targeted, often experiencing significant financial loss along with shame, anxiety, and social isolation. Through workshops delivered by MediaSmarts experts participants will learn how AI-enabled scams work, how to verify messages from family or financial institutions, and what steps to take if targeted.

opportunities.title: How We Stay Relevant in the Age of AI
opportunities.description: AI is changing how people think about work, learning, and human value. Many professionals, parents, students, and community members are asking a very real question: if AI can generate answers, summaries, explanations, drafts, code, and ideas so quickly, where do humans remain relevant? This session argues that humans should not try to compete with AI at speed, recall, or routine output. That is the wrong competition. As AI makes answers easier to produce, human value moves toward deeper understanding, disciplined curiosity, judgment, and the ability to question, verify, and ground what AI produces. For most of us, learning has often been treated as natural and implicit. We were taught subjects in school, but not always taught how learning itself works. Machine learning gives us a useful mirror. In order to teach machines how to learn, humans had to make parts of learning explicit: objectives, data, patterns, prediction, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating. This session uses those machine learning principles not as a technical lesson, but as a way to think about how humans can learn more deeply in the age of AI. Participants will explore why superficial knowledge is becoming less survivable, why AI still needs to be grounded in human reality, and how disciplined curiosity can help people remain valuable as AI becomes more capable. The session will include a short lecture-style presentation followed by a guided audience discussion. The discussion can be shaped around a small number of reflection questions, with flexibility to shift into Q&A or a brief example/demo depending on the audience engagement and MPL’s preference. No technical background is required. By the end of this session, participants will be able to: Explain why shallow learning and routine knowledge work become more vulnerable when AI can generate fluent answers quickly. Apply key machine learning principles, such as objective-setting, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating, as a practical framework for deeper human learning, better questioning, and stronger judgment. Bio: Darren Soo is a Canadian technology founder and creator of PI, an individualized AI reasoning framework designed to help people reason through complex, changing information over time. His background spans more than two decades of practical technology work across enterprise and operational software environments. His current work centres on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and explainable reasoning systems, while his broader interests include how technology can support curiosity, better questions, learning and decision-making.

opportunities.title: Vibe Coding: Create Programs and Apps using AI
opportunities.description: "Vibe Coding" is a coding approach that uses AI as your programming partner—no coding knowledge required! Using vibe coding, you can create apps, websites, and simple language simply by describing what you want. In this hands-on session, you'll learn to describe in simple language what you want and let the AI help create the code. You don't need any prior programming skills or experience at all! This is the perfect introduction to coding in the age of AI... all you need is curiosity and creativity! Note: There will be a hands-on component to this program so we highly recommend bringing a laptop or mobile device so you can try out what we've talked about on your own!

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Aaniin
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!
